overview.summary: A two-part meteorological platform pairing a FastAPI backend that enriches Open-Meteo data with a React single-page frontend. It combines a live dashboard, a natural-language weather assistant, IMD-aligned severe weather alerts, an interactive map, crop advisory, climate trends, and historical analog forecasting.
overview.problem: General weather apps report numbers without interpretation, and AI weather assistants tend to invent numbers that sound plausible but are not measured. Neither helps a farmer or traveller decide what to actually do.
overview.solution: Ground every number in observed or forecast data from Open-Meteo, then use language only to explain those numbers. Add decision-oriented modules for agriculture, hazards, and historical precedent.

corePrinciple.statement: All numeric weather facts originate from Open-Meteo. No language model ever produces a number.
corePrinciple.enforcement: The assistant fetches real data, extracts only the slice relevant to the question, and passes those verified values to the explainer. Without an LLM key configured, a deterministic template synthesiser produces the same response shape from the same verified numbers.

architecture.style: Layered client-server with resilient direct-to-provider fallback

layer.name: Presentation
layer.responsibility: Render views, handle interaction, localise all strings
layer.detail: Seven tab views plus shared layout and common components

layer.name: API Client
layer.responsibility: Single point of contact with the backend
layer.detail: For most calls it tries the FastAPI backend first, and on network failure, a non-400 error, or a 5xx it falls back to calling Open-Meteo directly from the browser. This keeps the dashboard usable when the backend is down.
layer.tradeoff: The fallback duplicates weather-code mapping and summary logic client-side, so a change to the backend WMO mapping must be mirrored here.

layer.name: HTTP Routing
layer.responsibility: Validate query parameters and delegate to a service
layer.detail: Thin routers with a uniform error contract. Each translates ValueError to 400, RuntimeError to 502, and anything unexpected to 500.

layer.name: Domain Services
layer.responsibility: All meteorological logic and upstream integration
layer.detail: Seven services, each owning one domain and independently testable

layer.name: Configuration
layer.responsibility: Settings read from environment with sane defaults
layer.detail: Pydantic BaseModel (not BaseSettings) populated via os.getenv. Holds the three Open-Meteo base URLs and the optional LLM keys.

crossCutting.concern: Wide open, allow_origins set to all, configured in main.py
Four languages, all UI strings routed through a token dictionary
Uniform ValueError and RuntimeError to 400 and 502 mapping across every router
In-memory LRU with TTL in the archive service, shared by two features

flow.name: Standard forecast request
flow.step: User selects a location, or searches a city via the geocoding endpoint
Frontend calls GET /api/weather/forecast with lat, lon, name
WeatherService calls Open-Meteo forecast API
WMO weather codes are mapped to label, icon, and category
Response is shaped into current, hourly, daily, and a summary sentence
On backend failure the client falls back to calling Open-Meteo directly

flow.name: Grounded assistant query
flow.step: QueryEntityExtractor regex-parses the free-text question
It resolves a location override, a timeframe bucket, and an intent category
WeatherService fetches real forecast data for the resolved location
AlertEngine classifies that forecast into any active hazards
_extract_weather_slice pulls only the verified numbers for the requested timeframe
_generate_grounded_explanation explains those exact numbers, forbidden from inventing values
If no LLM key is set, _grounded_deterministic_synthesis templates the same answer per intent
Both paths return an identical JSON shape
flow.returns: answer, badge, rating, key_facts, action_advice, suggested_followups

flow.name: Historical analog matching
flow.step: ArchiveService fetches or serves from cache a 41-year daily record for the location
Today's six-feature fingerprint is read from the forecast API
Candidates are gated to plus or minus 10 circular days of today's day-of-year across all years
Features are z-scored across the candidate pool and compared by weighted Euclidean distance
Matches are selected best-first with a 7-day minimum separation so each is a distinct episode
For each match, the following 7 days are read from the archive
Aggregates and a deterministic verdict sentence are computed

feature.name: Weather Deja Vu
feature.description: Finds historical days whose atmospheric state resembles today, then shows what actually happened in the seven days after each one.
feature.novelty: Analog forecasting is an established meteorological technique that is essentially never surfaced to end users. Consumer weather apps report a probability; this reports the empirical precedent behind it.
feature.example: Chennai, 5 September 2026: eight of the eight closest matches across 41 years were raining within 72 hours, the following week averaged 41.1mm.

algorithm.name: Historical Analog Matching
algorithm.purpose: Answer what usually follows a day like today, using this location's own record

step.name: Seasonal gate
step.detail: Candidates restricted to plus or minus 10 days of today's day-of-year, across all archive years. Day-of-year distance is circular, so 31 December and 2 January are 2 days apart, not 364.
step.rationale: Load-bearing. Without it a warm January day could match an August monsoon day on temperature and humidity alone, and the resulting outcome would describe dynamics that cannot occur in January.
step.result: Approximately 861 candidates for a typical location

step.name: Fingerprint
step.rationale: Precipitation is log-transformed because it is zero-inflated and long-tailed; raw values would let a single extreme day dominate the metric. Weights are ordered by consequence to a decision-maker.
step.note: Today's fingerprint comes from the forecast API because the archive lags about five days. The same six variables are read from both sources so the vectors are directly comparable.

step.name: Distance
step.detail: Features z-scored across the candidate pool, then weighted Euclidean distance
step.rationale: Standardising against the candidate pool rather than the whole archive sets the scale by seasonally comparable days

step.name: Diverse selection
step.detail: Matches taken best-first, skipping any within 7 days of one already chosen
step.rationale: Without this the top matches cluster inside a single historical weather episode. In testing, three of the top eight were the same 2015 week, and their near-identical aftermaths inflated every aggregate. Adding the separation changed the Hyderabad rain-within-72-hours figure from 50 percent to 25 percent; the original was wrong.

step.name: Similarity score
step.caveat: A relative closeness measure against a typical day at this location and season. It is not a probability, and the interface says so explicitly.

step.name: Outcome window
step.detail: Days plus 1 to plus 7 read from the archive for each selected match
Matches without a complete, calendar-contiguous window are discarded before ranking, never truncated
step.rationale: A partial window would silently bias aggregates downward

outputs.output: Share of matches with at least 1mm inside three days
Average total of the following week
Average temperature change by day three
Template-generated sentence, computed values only, no LLM

algorithm.name: Grounded Query Resolution
algorithm.step: Regex entity extraction for location override, timeframe bucket, and intent
Real forecast fetch for the resolved location, geocoding first if another place is named
Slice extraction limited to the requested timeframe's hour range
Explanation from verified numbers, via LLM or deterministic template
algorithm.constraint: The explainer is instructed to explain these exact numbers and never invent values

algorithm.name: Archive Caching
algorithm.detail: Keyed on coordinates rounded to 0.1 degrees, roughly 11km, approximating the provider's own grid
algorithm.rationale: Finer keys would spend cache slots on identical upstream data
algorithm.detail: Rows with a null in any required field are dropped at load, so consumers may assume complete records
algorithm.impact: Shared by both the analog engine and the climate service, so one fetch serves two features

weatherCodes.categories: clear, cloudy, fog, drizzle, rain, heavy-rain, snow, thunderstorm

localisation.convention: No UI string is inlined; every string routes through the token dictionary

coverage.note: The repository has no test framework. Verification is by direct endpoint probe.

decision.title: Numbers never come from a language model
decision.rationale: An LLM that invents a rainfall figure is worse than no answer, because it is confidently wrong
decision.consequence: Two explanation paths, LLM and deterministic, returning an identical shape

decision.title: Client falls back to the provider when the backend is down
decision.rationale: Keeps the dashboard usable in degraded conditions
decision.consequence: Weather-code mapping is duplicated client-side and must be kept in sync

decision.title: The analog endpoint deliberately has no client fallback
decision.rationale: The analog computation is the feature. Reimplementing it in TypeScript would duplicate a non-trivial algorithm in two languages and contradict the project's own warning about keeping duplicated logic in sync.
decision.consequence: On backend failure the view shows an explanatory empty state

decision.title: One archive layer serves both analog and climate
decision.rationale: Both features need the same long record; a shared cache means one fetch serves two features

decision.title: Climate normals use the 1991-2020 WMO reference period
decision.rationale: The conventional baseline means departure percentages carry their usual meteorological meaning

decision.title: Analogs must be seven days apart
decision.rationale: Guarantees each match is an independent weather episode rather than one event sampled repeatedly

knownIssues.issue: Mobile horizontal overflow: the header's control cluster does not wrap, producing about 592px of content in a 390px viewport. Pre-existing and present on every tab.
LLM_PROVIDER is defined in settings but never consulted. Provider choice is determined by which API key is present.
The production bundle exceeds the 500 KB warning threshold at 859 KB raw. Code splitting would address it.

The Open-Meteo free tier rate limits repeated cold archive fetches with HTTP 429. The cache makes this rare in normal use; the error is surfaced distinctly so users know to wait rather than assume the location is unsupported.
